intro: Zelve Open Air Museum, in Nevşehir province, is a rock settlement whose story runs from the 9th century AD to 1952. Spread over three valleys, it was lived in without a break until 1952, when the danger of collapse emptied it.
history: Spread over three valleys, Zelve was one of the places where Cappadocia's Christian and Muslim inhabitants lived side by side in the same rock: rock-cut churches in one valley, a rock-cut mosque in another. Then, in the 1950s, the cliffs began to crack and fall, and the village was evacuated to New Zelve, two kilometres away.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Fish Church and the Grape Church, then the Rock-cut mosque. Look out, too, for the Mill and the Tunnels.
facts: Did you know? Zelve is one of the few Cappadocian settlements whose abandonment has an exact date: the village was cleared in 1952, so some of the people who lived in it are still alive. It is also one of the few places where a rock-cut church and a rock-cut mosque stand side by side in the same cliff. And why was it left? Because the rock was starting to collapse.
outro: This brings our tour of Zelve Open Air Museum to an end. Before you go, please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. Thank you for listening to the story of this valley, and enjoy your visit.
